facts.statement: Campinasuchus fossils come from four partial skulls found in the Honorópolis District of the Adamantina Formation, dating to between 93.5 and 83.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Campinasuchus is known from four partial skulls from the Honorópolis District of the Adamantina Formation, Bauru Basin, dating to the Turonian or the Santonian stage of the late Cretaceous, about 93.5-83.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus Campinasuchus was first named in 2011 by a team including Ismar De Souza Carvalho and Vicente De Paula Antunes Teixeira.
facts.quote: Campinasuchus was first named by Ismar De Souza Carvalho, Vicente De Paula Antunes Teixeira, Mara Lúcia Da Fonseca Ferraz, Luiz Carlos Borges Ribeiro, Agustín Guillermo Martinelli, Francisco Macedo Neto, Joseph J. W. Sertich, Gabriel Cardoso Cunha, Isabella Cardoso Cunha and Partícia Fonseca Ferraz in 2011

facts.statement: The generic name Campinasuchus combines 'Campina' from the location of discovery and 'suchus', referring to the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Campina in reference to Campina Verde County in which Campinasuchus was found, and suchus, Latinized from the Greek souchos, an Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.

facts.statement: The species name 'diniz' honors Izonel Queiroz Diniz Neto and the Diniz and Martins Queiroz families, who owned the farm where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the owners of the farm where the specimens were excavated: Izonel Queiroz Diniz Neto and the families Diniz and Martins Queiroz.

facts.statement: Campinasuchus was a fully terrestrial predator, similar to other baurusuchids.
facts.quote: Campinasuchus, like other baurusuchids, was a fully terrestrial predator.

facts.statement: Campinasuchus possessed a deep, laterally compressed skull equipped with large, blade-like teeth.
facts.quote: It had a deep and laterally compressed skull with large, blade-like teeth.

facts.statement: Unlike other baurusuchids, Campinasuchus had a very short and low snout.
facts.quote: Compared to other baurusuchids, it has a very short, low snout.

facts.statement: The upper margin of Campinasuchus's skull was lower than the back of the skull, creating a slightly sloping profile distinct from other baurusuchids.
facts.quote: Its upper margin is also lower than the back of the skull, giving the head a slightly sloping profile (other baurusuchids have high snouts that are level with the rest of the skull).

facts.statement: A small pit on the premaxilla of Campinasuchus accommodated the first tooth of the lower jaw when the jaws were closed.
facts.quote: A small pit on the premaxilla accommodates the first tooth of the mandible when the jaws are closed.

facts.statement: Campinasuchus had relatively small supratemporal fenestrae, or holes at the back of the skull.
facts.quote: The supratemporal fenestrae, holes at the back of the skull, are relatively small.

facts.statement: Campinasuchus belongs to the parent group Pissarrachampsinae.
Campinasuchus is classified within the family Baurusuchidae.
Campinasuchus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Campinasuchus is an extinct genus of baurusuchid mesoeucrocodylian from Minas Gerais State of Brazil.
